ko.executive_summary: AI data center infrastructure investment continues to accelerate, with a projected $17B bet through 2026, while power delivery innovation intensifies. STMicroelectronics reports surging AI data center bookings in Q3 FY2026, and Lite-On Technology is positioning 800 VDC power architecture for AI chip applications. However, emerging anti-data center sentiment poses regulatory and operational risks to expansion plans.
key_facts: $17B AI data center investment projected through 2026
STMicroelectronics Q3 FY2026 AI data center bookings surge
Lite-On Technology 800 VDC power delivery architecture
electronica Munich event venue for power delivery announcements

implications.text: 800 VDC architecture represents shift toward higher voltage standards for AI chip power efficiency; critical for CPO thermal and integration challenges in dense data center deployments.
STMicroelectronics and Lite-On activity indicates consolidated supplier focus on AI infrastructure; optical interconnect vendors must align power and thermal specs with 800 VDC systems.
Anti-data center sentiment threatens capex acceleration; CPO adoption timelines may slip if facility deployment faces local/state opposition.

ko.counterpoint: Political opposition to data center expansion may constrain near-term capex deployment despite strong component-level booking signals from major chipmakers.
